subject: respiratory-therapy
intro: Respiratory therapy leads into the bedside specialties that manage the airway and the breath — ventilators in intensive care, oxygen in the ward, rehab in the clinic — and into the nursing teams they work beside.

roles.title: Respiratory Therapists
roles.what: Assess, treat and care for patients with breathing disorders, taking primary responsibility for respiratory care: selecting, assembling and operating the equipment, running the therapies and keeping the records.
roles.where: The TMC domains are the job: unit 1's blood gas interpretation, unit 2's oxygen delivery devices, unit 3's airway management and unit 4's ventilator modes, ARDS protective ventilation and weaning.

roles.title: Exercise Physiologists
roles.what: Assess, plan and implement exercise programmes that improve cardiorespiratory function and fitness, often for patients recovering from heart and lung disease.
roles.where: Unit 5's pulmonary rehabilitation — COPD and asthma pathophysiology with bronchodilator therapy — plus unit 1's cardiopulmonary assessment are exactly the knowledge base this role runs on.

roles.title: Registered Nurses
roles.what: Assess patient health problems and needs, develop and implement nursing care plans, and administer care to ill, injured and recovering patients across wards, critical care and community settings.
roles.where: Unit 6's critical care monitoring and neonatal resuscitation, and unit 1's patient assessment and data, are the shared ground between the respiratory team and the nursing staff it works beside.
